report: Cross-verse: no split found. הוּא Sp3mp in 58.4 takes Their…They because the ASV resumes the suffix's referent in a later verbless clause of the same verse (rules 18/25); 58.6 has no resumption. Sp3ms her/them are different suffixes with different referents.

כְּמוֹ: as (58.7), are like / is like (58.4, prepositional predicate, rule 49), Let…be as (58.8) and let…be as though (58.7) are all the same rule-49 copula placement with different English frames; 58.9's alike/and are the two halves of the correlative כְּמוֹ…כְּמוֹ rendered 'X and Y alike' — second particle stands where the ASV's connective stands (rule 26's reasoning), first takes the postposed alike. One verse, not a chapter pattern.

לְ Rd→Td: For (title dedication, 58.0) vs there is for (verbless-clause predicate with presentative frame, 58.11) is a construction difference; both R→Sp3mp cases are unrepresented (possessive recast 58.4, ethical dative 58.7), consistent.

Supplied subject pronouns are consistent under rule 25's verse scope: They (58.4) and them (58.7 second colon) join a written nominal that denotes the referent; them of 58.8 'Let them be as a snail' is added because the verse writes no nominal for the wicked; them of 58.7 'Let them melt' is the 3mp verb's own (rule 17).

Supplied relatives are consistent: that (58.4), that/When (58.7), which/that (58.8) are added over asyndetic finite clauses juxtaposed to written antecedents (rules 46/55); that judgeth (58.11) stays with the postnominal articleless participle (rule 41). One available alternative not taken in 58.8: which could be read as the construct relation of שַׁבְּלוּל תֶּמֶס realized as a relative (rules 19/46) rather than added; the verse pass's reading is defensible because the same relative also encloses the finite יַהֲלֹךְ, so it is left as accepted and recorded here.

Remaining single-occurrence candidates (אֱלֹהִים, אָדָם, דָבַר, הָלַךְ, חֵמָה, חָזָה, צַדִּיק, רָשָׁע, שָׁפַט) are the ASV rendering one word in different syntactic positions; supplied the/a/of placements follow rules 15, 19, 29, 46 uniformly across the chapter.

BSB disagreements: three paragogic nuns (58.1, 58.2 ×2) are the rule-32 convention; the ethical dative לָמוֹ of 58.7 (preposition and suffix) is the rule-40 convention where BSB attaches the dative to its verb. None is an error; no edge changed.

Head choices noted but not changed: 58.0 Chief Musician headed on Musician (Chief was the competing head; rule 31's tie-break could point either way and earlier Psalm titles should govern), 58.9 whirlwind, 58.6 teeth — each unit names its competitor under rule 8.

Conventions: the eight repeated notes each restate a contract rule (12, 15, 17, 18, 29, 32, 46), so none is recorded. No promotion: the correlative כְּמוֹ…כְּמוֹ → 'and … alike' rests on a single verse and the corpus shows only DEU.5.14 כָּמוֹ → as well as as a one-unit analogue, which is not enough to generalise.
